# SaneHosts

> SaneHosts is a Mac app that blocks ads, trackers, malware and distracting sites system-wide by managing the Mac's built-in hosts file. No VPN, no cloud account, no subscription. Pick one of five protection levels or build profiles from 30 curated blocklists. You approve its helper once in System Settings; after that, changes apply without a password prompt. $14.99 once after a 14-day trial (no credit card). macOS 14 Sonoma or later. Made by SaneApps.

## Facts
- Current version: 1.1.27 (direct download)
- Price: $14.99 one-time after a 14-day trial with every feature, no card. Also in the SaneApps Bundle ($49.99 once).
- Install: direct download from sanehosts.com, or Homebrew `brew install --cask sane-apps/tap/sanehosts`. It's a direct download, not Mac App Store, because writing the system hosts file needs local system access.
- Requirements: macOS 14.0 Sonoma or later
- Privacy: hosts data stays on your Mac. No cloud account, no personal-content upload.
- Listed in the StevenBlack/hosts README (third-party tools). Source code public on GitHub (github.com/sane-apps/SaneHosts), PolyForm Shield licence.

## Protection levels
- Essentials (~230K entries): ads, trackers, malware
- Family Safe (~315K): Essentials + adult content and gambling
- Focus Mode (~320K): Family Safe + social media
- Privacy Shield (~355K): Focus Mode + telemetry and advanced trackers
- Kitchen Sink (~500K): everything available

## Features
- 30 curated blocklists (Steven Black, Hagezi, AdGuard and more), import from files and URLs
- Unlimited profiles (work, family, focus); merge, duplicate, switch from the menu bar
- Works in every app (Safari, Chrome, Slack, games), not just browsers
- Allowed Sites: unblock a site a list breaks, on every profile, subdomains included (right-click any entry, Always Allow)
- Update Now on list-based profiles, plus a weekly update of the active profile; a failed download changes nothing
- Import a hosts file from your Mac or an HTTPS list
- Optional Touch ID lock: turning protection off, switching profiles, editing the active profile and changing Allowed Sites ask for Touch ID or the Mac password
- Automatic DNS cache flush on every change; automatic backups and rollback
- No Terminal needed

## Limits (honest)
- Hosts blocking works by domain: it can't block ads served from the same domain as the content, and it doesn't hide empty ad boxes inside web pages.
- Mac only.
